tool_input.body:
## Summary

Closes the four bugs left over from the session-identity triage cluster after DES-074 shipped in v4.17.0. Small, independent, same subsystem.

**`ethos-lldo`** — `plugin/hooks/commit-msg.sh`'s header claimed "Passthrough when neither env var is set", while the body did a full session lookup on exactly that branch. That lookup is where cross-repo misattribution entered, so the header actively steered a reader away from the live defect. Rewritten to describe what the code does, including DES-074's split: a named error under Claude Code when the session is unresolvable, silent when not under Claude Code.

**`ethos-4pvt`** — `session end` now prints `unset ETHOS_SESSION` when the variable is set. The asymmetry was that `session start` prints the export, so the command that *sets* it told you and the command that *invalidates* it didn't.

The bead's filed symptom turned out to be stale: it said a leftover export later reports "not found". DES-074 already changed that — it now fails loud with `ErrNoSession` rather than silently degrading to the git identity. Added a regression pinning that too, so the corrected behaviour can't quietly revert.

**`ethos-gu3p`** — `session start --persona <unknown>` exited 0 and wrote a roster keyed on a handle resolving to no identity; the typo then never surfaced, because lookups fell through to the git identity. Now validated before anything is minted or written. Test asserts non-zero exit **and** zero new files in the sessions dir — the bead's real complaint was the dangling artifact, not just the exit code.

Deliberately scoped to `session start`, **not** `iam`: several existing tests key participants on free-form labels with no backing identity by design (`TestRunIam_UpdatesLegacyKeyedParticipant`, the concurrent-join race), so validating there breaks legitimate uses that `session start --persona` doesn't have.

**`ethos-cm2r`** — added `internal/process/proc_windows.go` using `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`, mirroring the pattern `x/sys` uses for its own `Getppid()`. No new module dependency — `x/sys` is already direct via the darwin sysctl file. Also hardened `isClaudeComm` for backslash paths, `.exe`, and case.

## What cm2r did *not* close, and why that's new information

`GOOS=windows go build ./...` still fails — one layer deeper, not in `internal/process`. `internal/session`'s flock-based `Store` is entirely `!windows`-tagged with no Windows implementation, so every consumer now fails on that missing symbol instead.

That needs a real file-locking primitive (`LockFileEx` or similar), not a stub, and it is bigger than either cm2r or `ethos-qtp2`. It also means **qtp2 stays unverifiable** until it closes, since `internal/mission` imports `internal/session` directly. Filed separately rather than scope-crept into this PR.

## Verification

Detached CI simulation — clean `git archive` extraction, all `CLAUDE_*` stripped: **27 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 no-test-files** (`internal/repomiss`, pre-existing).

`make check` green after every commit. Each new test verified failing against pre-fix code before the fix landed.

Windows: `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./internal/process/...` and `go vet` both clean; linux/darwin builds and `internal/process` tests unaffected.

CHANGELOG entries for the two user-visible changes (4pvt, gu3p). None for the header comment or the Windows work — Windows isn't a supported target.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

tool_input.content:
`internal/session`'s `Store` is entirely `//go:build !windows`-tagged with no Windows implementation, so `GOOS=windows go build ./...` fails on the missing symbol in every consumer: `internal/resolve`, `internal/mission`, `internal/hook`, `internal/mcp`, `cmd/ethos`.

## How it surfaced

Found while closing `ethos-cm2r` (2026-09-07). That bead was scoped to `internal/process` being darwin/linux-only, and it is now fixed — `proc_windows.go` uses `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`, and `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./internal/process/...` is clean.

Fixing it moved the failure one layer down rather than resolving the full build. `internal/process` is off the list; `internal/session` is now the blocker.

## Why this is not a stub job

The `Store` uses flock for cross-process concurrency on the session roster — that is load-bearing, not incidental. Two sessions writing a roster concurrently is the normal case, and the DES-074 work depends on the pointer file and roster being written atomically under a lock. A stub that no-ops the locking would compile and then corrupt rosters under exactly the concurrency the package exists to handle.

The real fix is a Windows locking primitive — `LockFileEx`/`UnlockFileEx` via `x/sys/windows`, which is already a direct dependency. That is a genuine implementation with its own failure modes (mandatory vs advisory semantics, handle lifetime, no `flock`-style upgrade), not a tagging exercise.

## Blocks

`ethos-qtp2` — `internal/mission` does not compile under `GOOS=windows` because untagged files reference symbols defined only in its `!windows` files. That bead **cannot be verified or its fix confirmed** until this one closes, because `internal/mission` imports `internal/session` directly, so the build never reaches mission's own errors. Same relationship `cm2r` had to `qtp2` before this.

Order is therefore: `cm2r` (done) → this bead → `qtp2`.

## Scope note

Windows is not a supported target today, which is why this is P3 and why `cm2r` was too. Filed so the boundary is recorded accurately rather than leaving `qtp2` looking actionable when it is not. Anyone picking up Windows support should expect further layers behind this one — each fix so far has revealed the next.

## Related

- `ethos-cm2r` — `internal/process` windows support (closed by this work)
- `ethos-qtp2` — `internal/mission` windows build, blocked behind this
- ethos PR #507 — where this was found

tool_input.content: PR #507 is up and pushed. Three review findings, …
tool_input.message:
PR #507 is up and pushed. Three review findings, all real, two of them defects in the fixes we just wrote. Fix on the same branch, do not push, report and I push.

**A — our 4pvt fix has a bug. Two reviewers found it independently.** `cmd/ethos/session.go` ~L652-655.

The `unset ETHOS_SESSION` hint fires whenever the variable is non-empty, not only when it names the session that was actually ended. So `ethos session end --session A` while `ETHOS_SESSION` points at live session B deletes A and tells the operator to clear B — which is still valid and is supplying their active context. Outside Claude Code that export is the only remaining discovery channel, so following the advice destroys their session.

Bugbot notes the same function ALREADY refuses to drop the current-pointer in that case, so the correct condition is right there and the hint just doesn't use it. Emit the hint only when the env value identifies the session that was successfully ended. Regression: end session A with `ETHOS_SESSION=B` set, assert no hint; end the session the env var names, assert the hint.

This is worth pausing on. We fixed a bug about advice that doesn't help, and shipped advice that actively harms. Same defect class, one step over.

**B — our gu3p fix is too shallow.** `cmd/ethos/session.go`, the `identityStore().Exists(sessionStartPersona)` check.

`Exists` is only an `os.Stat`. It neither loads the record nor validates `kind`. So malformed YAML, a layered load error, a missing `kind`, or a `kind` that is neither `human` nor `agent` all pass the check, and the invalid handle still reaches roster creation and participant persistence — failing later at `whoami`, which is exactly the deferred-failure the bead was filed about.

Validate by LOADING the identity and checking it resolves to a valid record, not by stat. Extend the test: a persona whose file exists but is malformed, and one with a missing/invalid `kind`, must both be rejected before any roster write.

**C — proc_windows.go swallows walk errors.** The snapshot walk discards the real `Process32First`/`Process32Next` error; any failure falls out of the loop and is reported as "pid ... not found". That hides genuine Windows API failures behind a benign-looking message and makes session detection undebuggable. Preserve and return non-`ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES` errors; only `ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES` means "walked to the end without finding it".

PROCESS: failing test first for A and B, verified failing before the fix. `make check` green per commit. Then the detached gate — use the inline command I sent, PIPE through tee, report BOTH the `ok` count and the `FAIL` count. Re-verify `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./internal/process/...` after C.

I filed the deeper Windows blocker you found as **ethos-298s** (internal/session has no Windows Store, gates qtp2) and linked qtp2 behind it. Your call to stop at that boundary rather than attempt a locking primitive was right.
